formats.name: Recurring-cast mini sitcom (one situation per episode)
formats.what: The same two or three friends in every film, each film one self-contained situation with a cold open, an obstacle and a payoff. No recap, no 'previously'. The reference case is Bilt's 'Roomies': short episodes on its own account, almost no brand mention, two People's Voice Webby awards.
formats.why_it_works: Search results agree that episodic series with recurring characters are what Gen Z and millennials return for ('mini TV shows in the feed'). The viewer gets attached to people, not to a product, and the brand can stay out of the picture until the end. Each film still works for someone who has seen none of the others.
formats.fits_ai_video: Yes. Reference pictures keep the cast the same person. Keep the cast to two or three, one or two in frame per shot, and build each film from five to seven clips. The risk is drift in voice and clothes between episodes, so lock one outfit and one voice per character.

formats.name: Wordless gag: problem, look, simple payoff
formats.what: A physical situation told with no dialogue: someone struggles, a friend or a local reacts with a look, a simple action solves or tops it. The lineage is silent film through to Khaby Lame, who built the largest TikTok following without speaking.
formats.why_it_works: It needs no translation, so it travels across countries, and it survives sound-off viewing. Lame's own explanation, quoted in the coverage found, is that silent comedy is a language everybody understands. The laugh sits in the reaction face, not in a line. This is the format that most directly meets the 'twelve-year-old with the sound off' test.
formats.fits_ai_video: Yes, the best fit of all. A reacting face in a 4 to 6 second clip is what generated video does most reliably. Keep the business with objects coarse (dragging, carrying, sitting on a suitcase) and avoid anything that needs precise hands or an object passed between people.

formats.name: One-line situation caption plus acted moment ('When your friend...')
formats.what: One short line at the top states the situation ('When your friend says he knows a shortcut'), and three to five shots play it out. This is the standard grammar of relatable skits on TikTok and Reels, often labelled 'POV'.
formats.why_it_works: The viewer knows what the film is about in the first second, so nothing has to be worked out. Recognition ('that is us') is what drives the share and the tag. My own knowledge, not a search finding: for a second-language audience a plain 'When...' sentence is safer than 'POV', which is used loosely and confuses some viewers.
formats.fits_ai_video: Yes. The brief already allows exactly one top line. The caption carries the setup, so every generated clip can be a simple action or reaction. The picture must still tell the story without the line.

formats.name: Friend-group types ('every football trip has this friend')
formats.what: Each character is one clear type: the planner, the one who is always late, the over-packer, the one who sleeps anywhere, the one who makes friends with everyone. A film shows one type meeting one situation, or a quick run through all of them.
formats.why_it_works: People tag the friend who is that type, which is the strongest share motive in this age group (own knowledge). Clear types also make a character readable in two seconds with no dialogue, and they give a series a light thread without needing earlier episodes.
formats.fits_ai_video: Yes. One person, one trait, one 4 to 6 second shot is ideal. The types should be shown by action (asleep standing up, huge suitcase) and never by a label on screen. Limit to three types on screen to keep faces consistent.

formats.name: Expectation and reality (plan and what happened)
formats.what: Two beats with a hard cut: what they imagined, then what actually happened. The hostel in the mind and the bunk bed in reality, the quick walk to the stadium and the long way round.
formats.why_it_works: The whole joke is in the contrast between two pictures, so it reads with the sound off and with no text. It is short, loopable and kind when the 'reality' ends warm (the bad plan turns into the best part of the trip).
formats.fits_ai_video: Yes. It can be made with as few as two to four clips, and the hard cut hides the continuity problems of generated video. Give the two halves clearly different light or colour so no label is needed.

formats.name: First encounter with the local thing
formats.what: The visiting friends meet something ordinary to locals and new to them: the street food, the tram full of scarves, the local fan who teaches them the chant. The film is their faces discovering it, and it ends with visitors and locals together.
formats.why_it_works: Search finding: at the 2026 World Cup, videos of foreign fans reacting to everyday local life became a viral subgenre, and TikTok says fan perspectives and reactions outperformed plain highlights. It is warm by nature because nobody loses: the local is the generous one and the visitor is delighted. One UK survey found that going to local bars and meeting locals is the top draw of an away trip.
formats.fits_ai_video: Yes. It is a face reacting plus one local character, which is two people in frame. Keep signs and menus out of focus, and invent the food and the place so no real city or brand is implied.

formats.name: Race against the clock (will they make kick-off?)
formats.what: One goal, a string of small obstacles, a payoff at the gate. Running with a suitcase, the wrong platform, the long way round, then arrival as the roar starts.
formats.why_it_works: It is the oldest silent-film structure and the clearest one: want, obstacle, payoff, all in movement. Energy and music do the work, and the stake is understood by anyone who has ever been late for anything (own knowledge).
formats.fits_ai_video: Yes with care. Walking, running and dragging a suitcase are on the brief's 'works well' list. Use five or six short clips and keep the stadium as light, sound and blurred background. The crowd and the match itself stay off screen; the roar is heard, not shown.

formats.name: Trip-day montage cut on the beat ('come with us')
formats.what: The day in half a minute: alarm, airport, street, scarf, walk to the ground, the roar, the train home. This is what fan creators actually post. Search results name the YouTube channel Away Days, the TikTok creator EFL Girl and 'The GroundHopper', whose approach is to let the stadium atmosphere speak for itself.
formats.why_it_works: It delivers the feeling the brief asks for at the end ('I want a trip like that with my friends') and it is the native form of real away-day content, so it does not read as an advert. Music carries it.
formats.fits_ai_video: Partly. Technically easy, since each beat is a 2 to 3 second cut from a generated clip. But it is a mood and not a story, so it fails the 'retell in one sentence' test when used alone. Use it as the texture inside a story film or as a closing run of three or four shots, never as the whole film.

truths: The alarm at four in the morning: one friend is already dressed with the scarf on and wide awake, the others cannot open their eyes.
One friend arrives with a huge suitcase for a single night, another with only a small backpack.
At the airport at dawn you see a stranger in the same colours and you nod at each other like old friends.
Everybody falls asleep on each other on the early flight or train, and one friend takes the photo.
The hostel bunk beds: the race for the top bunk, the friend who snores, tiptoeing in the dark.
You do not need a map to find the stadium: you get off and follow the scarves and the noise.
The 'shortcut' of one friend that puts you on the wrong side of the stadium, so you walk all the way round.
The first sight of the stadium or its floodlights between the buildings: everyone goes quiet, then grins.
The scarf seller outside the ground: you said you would not buy one, and you walk away wearing it.
The food from a stand outside the ground that you would never eat at home, and it is the best meal of the trip.
Ordering with three words of the local language and a lot of pointing, and the seller answers in perfect English.
The phone at three percent exactly when you need it, and the friend with the power bank becomes the hero.
The ticket check: you hold your breath until the gate lets you through, then celebrate as if it were a goal.
Coming up the steps and the green pitch opens in front of you: the same face on everyone, every time.
The chant you do not know: you clap a beat late and move your lips, then a local teaches you and by the end you are the loudest.
The goal goes in and you hug a complete stranger.
The friend who went to get food and missed the goal, hearing the roar from the corridor.
The weather you did not plan for: half a sunburned face, or the thin rain poncho that everyone ends up wearing.
Swapping scarves and taking a photo with a local fan after the match.
The next morning nobody has a voice left, so the whole group talks in croaks and gestures.
The train home: everyone asleep in their scarves, one still humming the chant, and somebody already planning the next trip.
vibe_notes: Look, young: daylight and golden hour, warm saturated colour, the camera close to faces and moving with the people, slightly imperfect framing as if a friend is filming. Search results agree that lo-fi signals (film grain, camcorder and digicam feel, jump cuts, visible mess) read as human in 2026 and that glossy, over-polished production is losing ground. TikTok's own 2026 trend report puts 'real experiences over curated perfection' first.

Look, the choice between photoreal and stylised: two search findings point the same way. A Bentley and Gallup survey reports 73% of Gen Z adults find it unacceptable for brands to use AI to create people or voices in ads, and Gen Z is described as quick to spot AI imagery. The AI series 'Fruit Love Island', with openly artificial stylised characters and a serial story, drew hundreds of millions of views. My inference (no search result compared the two directly): a designed, stylised look that does not pretend to be real people is the safer route than photoreal humans. Make it tactile and warm (clay or felt feel, chunky shapes, sunlight), not a glossy plastic studio-film copy and not flat corporate vector art.
Light: sun, open sky, colour in clothes and streets. Night scenes, dim rooms and grey grading are what made the first series feel like true crime.

Music: the track leads and the cuts land on the beat. Search returned no reliable genre data, so this is my own knowledge: what reads young and international in 2025 and 2026 is warm, percussive dance music around 115 to 130 beats per minute (afro house and amapiano drums, the garage and two-step revival, Brazilian funk bounce, Latin and afrobeats rhythm), with one hook you can hum. For this series a clap pattern and a group 'oh-oh' vocal that could be sung in a stand would tie the theme to football. One analysis of 3.3 million videos found a rising share of TikTok videos using original sound, which supports a theme made for the series.
Sound: natural sound sells the place as much as the picture does. A muffled roar through concrete, a station hall, suitcase wheels on stone, a laugh that is not cut clean.

Pacing: start in the middle of the action with the problem already visible in the first one to two seconds. No logo, no title card, no slow establishing shot. A cut roughly every two to three seconds, the payoff in the last three seconds, and an ending that loops back to the start. Shorter is better: 20 to 30 seconds holds better than 40.

Captions: large bold sans-serif in sentence case, two to five words at a time, placed in the middle-lower safe area, looking like the platform's own text and not like a designed broadcast graphic. At most one word in an accent colour. Slow enough that a second-language viewer never has to choose between reading and watching (my own knowledge; search found no sourced caption guidance).

Performance: people who are clearly enjoying each other. Laughter, teasing that ends in a hug, small real imperfections (creased shirt, crumbs, messy hair). Mixed group, women as fans and not as decoration: one source names a woman, EFL Girl, as the leading away-day creator on TikTok.

Brand presence: the model that works is a series with almost no brand in it. 'Roomies' ran on its own account with no brand mention and viewers returned weekly. One survey reports 81% of Gen Z say they can tell when content is an ad, and the moment a voice sounds like a brand they leave.

Reads as dated: all-capitals yellow meme text, word-by-word caption pop with an emoji on every line (the 2022 to 2023 style), typewriter and glitch effects, whoosh sound effects on every cut, 'wait for it', a pile of hashtags (posts with more than five have nearly vanished according to one analysis).

Reads as corporate or as an advert: a logo in the first frame, a drone shot of the city, slow-motion friends laughing with perfect teeth and brand-new clothes, a narrator, a slogan, 'link in bio', a phone screen held to camera, brand colours on everything, cheerful stock music with whistling and ukulele or big trailer drums, and youth slang that sounds written by a committee.
avoid: Stories that must be read: chat screenshots, signs, documents, counters, fast captions. If the picture does not tell it with the sound off, it is not told.
Irony, deadpan, mock documentary and subtext. Also jokes that need an earlier episode, and cliffhangers that leave a single film unfinished.
Humiliation and 'cringe' humour. Never make the fan who does not know the chant, or the local, the target. The laugh is with them and the ending is warm.

Photoreal AI people presented as if real, and any AI content posted without the platform's AI label. Surveys found in search show strong Gen Z hostility to AI-made people and voices in ads, and 'Fruit Love Island' lost 12 of 22 episodes after reports that cited unlabeled AI and fake engagement.

The known weak spots of generated video: readable text in the picture, crowds in focus, match action, hands doing precise work with tickets or phones, objects passed hand to hand, mirrors, more than three people who must stay consistent.

Aggression of any kind: hooligan and ultras posturing, flares, pitch invasions, rival fans as enemies. Search shows this content exists on TikTok (the 'junior hooligan' niche, the concourse party crowd) but it is the opposite of the tone asked for and a risk for a brand.

Alcohol as the joke. The airport beer at six in the morning is a true British away-day moment, but drinking-centred humour narrows an international audience and can limit distribution on the platforms. Use food and coffee.
Real clubs, badges, recognisable kit colour pairs, real stadiums, cities, players, rivalries and brands. Also national stereotypes about the hosts. Never the word 'soccer'.
Slang of one country ('limbs', 'scenes', 'lads') and committee-written youth slang. Lines longer than about ten words.
Advert tells: logo or app before the last second, phone screen, price, slogan, narrator, call to action, a to-camera 'hey guys' opening.
Chasing a specific trending sound or meme format. It dates within weeks, and commercial use of trending music is a licensing problem for a brand account.
A montage with no story. Mood alone fails the 'retell it in one sentence' test.
Night, dim interiors, grey colour and middle-aged casts: the exact signals that made the first series feel serious.
Putting the punchline in a caption or in the end card instead of in the action on screen.

title: Match Day Diary
premise: Nina, 22 and football-mad, films a one-day trip to a match abroad with her two best friends on her front camera and tells us everything like a friend: in each film one small thing goes wrong, and it always ends with three happy faces squeezed into the frame.
look: STYLISED, not photoreal: warm hand-made 3D animation that looks like a clay-and-felt model film shot on a phone's front camera. CHARACTERS: slightly chunky proportions (head about one fifth of the body), big eyes and thick eyebrows that read on a small screen, matte clay-like skin with a soft thumbprint texture, hair like sculpted wool, clothes of felt, cotton and knitted wool with a visible weave, short rounded fingers. Motion is smooth, not jerky. PALETTE: coral, sunflower yellow, sky blue, mint, lilac and cream on pastel walls (peach, pistachio, butter) under a deep blue sky; shadows are warm violet, never black; no grey anywhere. LIGHT: daytime only, from morning gold to late-afternoon golden hour with a little lens flare; indoor places (hostel, train) are flooded with sun from a window. LENS: every shot comes from Nina's diary camera, in three ways only: (1) selfie, a wide front camera at arm's length (about 18 mm feel), her face in the upper half, her coral sleeve entering from the same bottom corner every time, a gentle hand wobble, friends and place readable behind her; (2) flip, the same camera turned round, seen from her low eye height; (3) handed over, a friend films her while walking backwards. No tripod beauty shots, no drone, no slow motion, and the phone is never seen because the lens is the phone. WARDROBE: one locked outfit per person in all films; the group scarf is plain coral-and-cream stripes with mint tassels; no letters, numbers or badges on anything. WORLD: an invented sunny city abroad with pastel houses, stone stairs, tram wires, flower pots and yellow-and-violet bunting (the home colours); shop signs are blank colour shapes; the stadium is only floodlight masts over roofs, a glow and a roar; other fans are soft blurred shapes in scarves. WHY: a to-camera diary made with photoreal people would be a fake vlogger, the thing this age group trusts least. An openly designed, hand-made look is honest and charming, is the opposite of the first series' grey realism, forgives lips, hands and skin, and its simple shapes and colour blocks keep each person identical from shot to shot.
music: Series theme "Oh-Oh" at 122 beats per minute: a warm afro-house groove with an amapiano-style log-drum bass, shakers, a bright four-note nylon-guitar riff, and handclaps in a stand pattern (clap-clap, clap-clap-clap). The hook is a group "oh-oh-oh-oh" sung by a few young mixed voices, with no words, so anyone can sing it in any language and it sounds like a stand. Every film uses the same shape: claps alone under the first shot, guitar and bass come in with the obstacle, one beat of silence at the turn, the full "oh-oh" chorus on the payoff, and the last clap lands on the end card. Feeling: sunny, bouncy, proud; something you add to a playlist and hum on the way to a ground. Natural sound is mixed as loud as the music (suitcase wheels on stone, steps, a tram bell, a far crowd, laughter that is not cut clean), and Nina sometimes hums the hook herself. No whistling, no ukulele, no trailer drums, no whoosh effects.

cast.name: Nina
cast.look: Small and quick, about 160 cm, light on her feet. Warm brown skin, round face, big dark-brown eyes, thick dark eyebrows that do half her talking, a few freckles across the nose, a wide smile with a small gap between the front teeth. Dark curly hair in two high round puffs, each tied with a coral scrunchie: this is her outline, readable at any size. Always the same clothes: an oversized plain coral football shirt with a cream collar and cream cuffs (no badge, no number, no words), light denim shorts, white trainers with coral laces, a tiny mint-green backpack, and the group scarf (coral and cream stripes, mint tassels, plain) loose round her neck. Her filming arm, coral sleeve with cream cuff, always enters the frame from the same bottom corner.
cast.personality: The one who keeps the diary. First awake, never tired until she suddenly is. She talks to the lens as if it were her best friend: she whispers secrets to it, gives it a wide-eyed look when something happens behind her, and laughs with her whole face. Very sure of herself ("I know the way"), often wrong, and happy to say so one second later. Filming her friends is how she shows she loves them. Voice: bright, quick, a little husky, a light non-native accent; one locked voice in every film.

cast.name: Otto
cast.look: Very tall and thin, about 193 cm, long arms and legs, bends down a little to hear his friends. Pale skin with freckles, cheeks that go pink in the sun, a white stripe of sun cream across his nose, soft fluffy ginger hair that stands up, gentle grey-green eyes, a slow wide smile. Always the same clothes: a sky-blue short-sleeved shirt worn open over a white T-shirt, sand-coloured shorts, white socks pulled up, white trainers, and the coral-and-cream scarf hanging straight down on both sides like a tie. His prop in every film: a sunflower-yellow hard suitcase on four wheels, as high as his chest and as high as Nina's chin, with a coral ribbon on the handle, no stickers, no text.
cast.personality: Ready for everything and quietly proud of it. Slow, calm, impossible to stop. Whatever anyone needs is somewhere in the yellow suitcase, and it is always for the others, never for himself. He does not argue when they laugh at him; he waits, and then he is right. His line is "You never know." Voice: soft, low, unhurried; one locked voice in every film.

cast.name: Yuki
cast.look: Small and compact, about 155 cm. Light skin with a warm tone, round face with full cheeks (usually full of food), calm dark eyes, a small smile at one corner of the mouth. Straight black hair in a blunt bob at jaw length with a short fringe and one butter-yellow clip on the left side. Always the same clothes: an oversized lilac windbreaker with the sleeves pushed up, a white T-shirt, wide cream trousers, chunky white trainers with lilac soles, a small butter-yellow belt bag worn across the chest (the snacks live there), and the coral-and-cream scarf wrapped twice round her neck. Nearly always holding something to eat.
cast.personality: Calm, hungry and never in a hurry. She says little, eats all the time and always holds the food out to share. Nothing surprises her, which makes her the perfect face next to Nina's big reactions. Her surprise: when the match starts she is the loudest of the three. She is also the one who takes the camera when Nina has to be in the picture. Voice: quiet and warm, with a sudden big laugh; one locked voice in every film.

why_clear: Every frame has two layers: Nina's face close to the lens shows how to feel, and the thing behind her shows what is happening, so the first frame already holds the whole situation (a laughing face and a giant yellow suitcase). Each film is about one bright object or one place that the eye can follow (a yellow suitcase, a wall, a scarf, a clap, a cone of fries, a sleeping friend), and the story is a physical turn-around of the same person: she laughs at the suitcase, then she rides on it. The steps are shown with big simple gestures (a thumb pointing back, a pat on the lid, a tap on the wrist, a slump on the kerb), never with text in the picture, a screen or a sign. Spoken lines are three to six everyday words said to the lens, and they only repeat what the picture already shows; the captions are those same words, large and slow, and there is one plain header line. Nothing depends on another film, on a tone of voice or on reading: with the sound off and the captions covered, the seven pictures still tell the story.
why_young_cool: It is the kind of video this audience makes and watches: a friend's trip filmed on the front camera, close, a little wobbly, starting in the middle of something, never with a "hey guys" opening. The people are three friends of 21 to 23 you would want to travel with, led by a football-mad young woman, and the fun comes from how they tease and then help each other; nobody is the fool, and every film ends with three laughing faces squeezed into one frame. Sun, pastel streets, colour-coded street clothes and a hand-made animated look feel fresh and nothing like an advert, and the look is honest about being made instead of pretending to be real people. The theme is a warm dance groove with a clap and an "oh-oh" you can sing in a stand. The brand is absent until the last second, so it plays as a show about friends, and the feeling it leaves is "I want that trip with my friends".

episodes.title: The Big Suitcase
episodes.story: Nina wants to move fast with her tiny backpack, but Otto has brought a giant yellow suitcase for one night and it slows them on every stair. When her own feet give up, he pats the lid, and she rides the suitcase down the street and tells the camera she loves it.

episodes.title: The Shortcut
episodes.story: Nina wants to reach the stadium first and leads the others down her "shortcut", filming herself marching in front. It ends at a high wall with the roar on the other side, so they walk all the way round, and on that long walk Yuki's nose finds a small food stand that becomes the best meal of the trip; Nina takes a bow for it.

episodes.title: No Scarf For Me
episodes.story: Nina tells the camera she will not buy a scarf because she already has one, and walks past the stand with a hand over her eyes while the old seller just smiles and holds one up. Hard cut: Nina in two scarves, a hat and a flag as a cape, and when she turns the camera round, Otto and Yuki are wearing the same.

episodes.title: I Don't Know This Song
episodes.story: On the walk to the ground the home fans are singing and Nina wants to join in, but she does not know the song: she claps one beat late and only moves her lips. A local fan her age sees it and teaches her the claps and the "oh-oh", and by the end Nina is the loudest of all and the local is the one filming her.

episodes.title: Yuki Gets Fries
episodes.story: Yuki wants fries, takes the camera and leaves the stand "for one minute"; alone in the sunny corridor with a full cone, she hears the roar of the goal she has just missed. She runs back to her hugging friends, and when the second roar comes she jumps so hard that the fries fly up and rain down on all three.

episodes.title: The Train Home
episodes.story: Nina wants one last diary film of everybody singing, but on the sunset train Otto and Yuki are asleep on each other in their scarves, so she films them in a whisper. Then her own eyes close, and the last shot is filmed by Yuki, awake and eating: Nina asleep with her mouth open, hugging the yellow suitcase.

pilot.title: The Big Suitcase
pilot.header: One night away. Otto brought a giant suitcase.
pilot.retell: Her friend brought a giant suitcase for a one-night trip and she laughed at it, but when she was too tired to walk she rode on it and loved it.

shots.place: A small square outside a train station in a sunny city abroad, early morning, low gold sun, long soft shadows, pastel houses.
shots.who: Nina close to the lens (selfie); Otto behind her with the suitcase.
shots.seen: Selfie. Nina's face fills the upper half of the frame, laughing, eyes wide; her arm reaches to the lens and a tiny mint backpack sits on her shoulder. Right behind her Otto walks up, waving, pulling a sunflower-yellow suitcase as high as his chest. In the first second Nina jerks her thumb back at the suitcase; then she holds up one finger to the lens.
shots.heard: NINA: "We are going for one night!" Natural sound: suitcase wheels rattling on stone, station hall hum, birds. Music: the claps alone.
shots.caption: We are going for one night! (the word "one" in coral)

shots.place: The same square, same morning light.
shots.who: Otto and the yellow suitcase (Nina is filming, not in frame).
shots.seen: The camera has turned round and looks up at Otto from Nina's height. He stands the suitcase upright beside him, puts one long arm round it like a friend, pats its top twice and lifts his chin, calm and proud.
shots.heard: OTTO: "You never know." Natural sound: two soft pats on the hard shell. Music: the guitar riff comes in.
shots.caption: You never know.

shots.place: Long stone stairs between pastel houses with flower pots, late morning, bright sun.
shots.who: Nina and Yuki close to the lens at the top; Otto small, lower down the stairs.
shots.seen: Selfie from the top of the stairs. Nina bounces on her toes, fresh and ready; next to her Yuki calmly eats a pastry. Far below them Otto pulls the yellow suitcase up one step at a time: it bumps, he stops, wipes his forehead, pulls again. Nina and Yuki turn their heads to watch him; then Nina looks back into the lens with raised eyebrows and taps her wrist.
shots.heard: None. Natural sound: bump... bump of the suitcase on stone, Otto puffing, Nina's short laugh. Music: the bass joins.
shots.caption: none

shots.place: A long straight street with trees and yellow-and-violet bunting, afternoon, hot bright sun.
shots.who: Nina; then the yellow suitcase and Otto's legs at the edge of the frame.
shots.seen: Selfie from low down. Nina sits slumped on the kerb, cheeks red, hair puffs drooping, fanning her face with the end of her scarf. She shakes her head at the lens. The yellow suitcase rolls into the frame beside her and stops; her eyes move to it.
shots.heard: NINA: "I can't walk any more." Natural sound: summer insects, wheels humming on smooth road and stopping. Music: drops back to the claps.
shots.caption: I can't walk any more.

shots.place: The same street, seen from the kerb looking up; blue sky, the sun behind Otto's head.
shots.who: Otto and the yellow suitcase (Nina is filming from the ground).
shots.seen: The camera looks up at Otto, tall against the blue sky. He rolls the yellow suitcase forward until it stands right in front of the lens, pats its flat top twice, the same pat as before, and raises his eyebrows with a small smile.
shots.heard: None. Natural sound: the same two pats. Music: one beat of silence.
shots.caption: none

shots.place: The same street, late afternoon, golden light, trees and bunting passing by.
shots.who: Nina and Otto (Yuki is filming, not in frame).
shots.seen: Filmed from the front by someone walking backwards. Nina sits on top of the upright yellow suitcase, legs kicking, both arms up, holding her scarf stretched above her head, mouth open in a happy shout. Otto runs behind, pushing the suitcase with both hands, laughing. They roll towards the camera while trees and bunting slide past and the sun flashes between the trees.
shots.heard: None. Natural sound: Nina's happy shout, wheels humming fast, Otto laughing. Music: the full "oh-oh" chorus.
shots.caption: none

shots.place: The same street a little further on, golden hour, warm light on the faces.
shots.who: Nina, Otto and Yuki.
shots.seen: Selfie from above, still rolling. Nina's glowing face is close to the lens, and under her we see the yellow lid she is sitting on. She pats the suitcase twice, exactly as Otto did. Otto leans in over her shoulder with a proud grin and points a thumb at himself; Yuki's face squeezes in from the other side, cheeks full. Three laughing faces fill the frame, with the yellow suitcase below them, the same picture as the first shot turned into a happy one.
shots.heard: NINA: "Okay. I love this suitcase." Natural sound: the pats, laughter that is not cut clean, a far crowd singing the same "oh-oh". Music: the last clap.
shots.caption: Okay. I love this suitcase.

pilot.end_card: About 1.5 seconds on plain coral: the word VENUVOY in cream letters, and under it one small line: "See you on the next trip." The last clap of the theme lands on it. No logo animation, no app, no link. Film plus end card runs about 30 seconds.

risks: The selfie arm: an arm reaching to the lens can stretch like rubber or grow extra fingers. Plan B: design the start still so that only a coral sleeve leaves the frame at the bottom corner, or frame chest-up with no arm at all; the wide lens and the hand wobble alone still say 'selfie'.

Character and style drift: faces, hair or the clay-and-felt texture change between clips, or the look turns glossy and plastic. Plan: approve one reference sheet per person first (front, three-quarter and selfie angle), lock one outfit, and start every clip from a designed still that already contains the approved person. Plan B: if the clay texture flickers, simplify to smooth matte 3D with the same shapes and colours.

Voices and lips: series one had voices that changed between films. Plan: one speaker per shot, three to six words per line, and one locked voice per person laid in from the same voice source for every film. Plan B: every line can be cut, because the film is built to work with no words; Nina's lines can also be placed over a flip shot where no lips are seen.

Shot 6, the ride: sitting on a rolling suitcase while someone pushes can produce sliding wheels, melting legs or a suitcase that changes size. Plan B: start the clip already in motion, keep it to 3 seconds and frame from the waist up so the wheels are out of frame and the moving background does the work. Plan C: drop shot 6 and let the high-angle selfie of shot 7 show the ride alone.

Shot 3 has three people (two near, one far) and the far Otto or the suitcase may lose shape or colour. Plan B: remove Yuki from this shot and introduce her only in the last one, or split it into two short shots: Otto alone on the stairs seen from Nina's flip view, then Nina's look to the lens.

The yellow suitcase is the hero object and must not change size, colour or ribbon. Plan: give it its own reference picture, keep it plain (no stickers, no text) and check its height against Otto's chest in every start still before animating.

The turn may not read with the sound off (why does she stop?). Plan B: make 'tired' bigger in the start still of shot 4: Nina flat on her back on the pavement like a star, scarf over her face, before the suitcase rolls in.

Garbled text and frame faults: scarves, shirts, bunting and shop signs can grow fake letters, and series one had a black band on a shot. Plan: plain stripes and blank colour shapes only, generate in native 9:16, and check every still and every clip edge to edge before it enters the edit. Shots 2 and 5 are generated as 4-to-5-second clips and trimmed.

The hand-made animated look could read as a children's show to viewers of 18 to 30. Plan: keep adult proportions and real street clothes, let the music and the teasing between friends carry the age, and test one still of the trio with people of the target age before any clip is made. Plan B: longer limbs, smaller eyes and less toy-like texture, still stylised and never photoreal.

The last shot squeezes three faces close to a wide lens, where a third face can drift. Plan B: two faces only (Nina and Otto) with Yuki's hand holding a pastry coming into the frame, which still gives the warm group ending.

title: Away Crew
premise: Maya plans everything, Kofi packs everything and Yuki worries about nothing: three friends from three countries on football trips abroad, one small problem per film, always solved together.
look: STYLISED, not photoreal: warm 3D animation with a handmade feel, like collectible art-toy figures living in a sunny miniature town. Skin is matte and clay-soft, clothes look like felt and knitwear with visible stitches, the suitcase is shiny plastic. Bodies have adult proportions and streetwear, heads only slightly large, eyes and eyebrows big enough to read on a phone; not a baby cartoon and not flat vector art. PALETTE: the world is peach, terracotta, cream stone, teal shutters and a cobalt sky. Each friend owns one colour (Maya cobalt blue, Kofi mint green plus his tangerine-orange suitcase, Yuki a cherry-red hat). All three wear the same knitted crew scarf in hot pink and sunflower yellow stripes, a colour pair that belongs to no real club. LIGHT: always sun, from late morning to golden hour, with long soft shadows; even the rain is a sun-shower; never night, never a dim room (interiors have big sunny windows). LENS: a virtual 28 to 35 mm camera held by hand at eye level, close to faces, a little wobble as if a fourth friend is filming, soft background, one simple move per shot (a push-in or a follow), full-frame 9:16, a cut every 2 to 4 seconds on the beat. WARDROBE: one outfit per person in every film, for ever; the scarf is worn three ways (Maya knotted short and neat, Kofi long and loose, Yuki wrapped twice). WORLD: an invented football town of stone steps, small squares, a little station, a hostel and food stands. It has no letters anywhere: signs are plain colour shapes and pictures. Locals are round, friendly older people in the same style. The stadium is only floodlights, a glow and a sound; crowds are soft shapes of colour. WHY: (1) it does not pretend to be real people, which is what young viewers reject in AI-made video; (2) it hides the weak spots of generated video: simple chunky hands, no text to garble, crowds as shapes, colour-blocked characters that stay the same person; (3) big faces make every reaction readable with the sound off; (4) it is the opposite of the first series at one glance: bright, young, playful.
music: One theme made for the series, working name 'Clap Clap'. Warm afro-house and amapiano-flavoured pop at 118 BPM in a major key. Instruments: a soft log-drum bass, shakers and congas, a bright clean four-note guitar riff, hand claps in the stadium pattern (clap-clap, clap-clap-clap), short brass stabs for the payoffs, and a small group of young mixed voices singing one wordless hook, 'oh-oh, oh-oh-oh', like a few friends in a stand. No lyrics, so nothing needs translating. Feeling: sun on your face on the walk to the ground; happy, bouncy, a little lazy. In every film: guitar and shaker start on frame one with no intro, the music dips under each spoken line, everything drops to a single shaker at the problem moment, the full hook with voices and brass lands on the payoff, and the last clap-clap hits the end card. No whistling, no ukulele, no trailer drums, no trending sound.

cast.name: Maya
cast.look: About 166 cm, slim and sporty, stands very straight, always half a step ahead of the others. Warm brown skin; oval face; thick straight black eyebrows that do most of her acting; large dark-brown eyes; small straight nose. Long black hair, always in one high tight ponytail held by a cobalt-blue scrunchie, two short wisps at the temples. Always wears: a cobalt-blue zip windbreaker with one white stripe across the chest (no letters), sleeves pushed up to the elbows; a white T-shirt; cream wide cargo trousers; white trainers; a chunky white sports watch with a blank face on the left wrist; a small flat white backpack worn high on both shoulders. Crew scarf (hot pink and sunflower yellow stripes) tied short and neat with one knot, like a tie. Her colour is cobalt blue.
cast.personality: Loves the plan more than the destination. Talks fast in short sentences, points with her whole arm, taps her watch, walks ahead and looks back. When the plan breaks her eyebrows shoot up; when things turn out well she is the first to hug and the loudest to laugh at herself. The biggest football fan of the three: missing kick-off is her only real fear. Voice: bright, quick, clear.

cast.name: Kofi
cast.look: About 192 cm, broad and soft, a big gentle bear who moves slowly. Deep dark-brown skin; round face with full cheeks; kind, slightly sleepy eyes; thick eyebrows; a wide slow smile; no beard. Short black hair in a neat high-top fade, flat on top and about four centimetres high, which gives him his outline. Always wears: an oversized mint-green hoodie with the hood down; stone-grey cargo shorts to the knee; white socks pulled up; chunky white trainers. Crew scarf hanging long and loose, both ends down his front. Always with him: 'Big Orange', a tangerine-orange hard-shell suitcase on four wheels, as tall as Maya's chest and as wide as Kofi himself, with a second crew scarf tied to its handle and no stickers or letters. His colours are mint green and the orange of the suitcase.
cast.personality: Calm, generous and prepared for everything; packing for the whole group is how he shows love. Speaks slowly and never says 'I told you so': he only smiles and says 'You never know.' Nothing embarrasses him and he is happy to be laughed with. Voice: deep, soft, smiling.

cast.name: Yuki
cast.look: About 155 cm, small and light, relaxed shoulders, never in a hurry. Light skin with a warm tone; round face; soft cheeks; half-closed happy eyes; a small constant smile. Black hair in a blunt chin-length bob with a straight fringe, always under a cherry-red bucket hat. Always wears: an oversized cream sweatshirt with sleeves down to her knuckles; wide light-blue jeans; white platform trainers with red socks. Crew scarf wrapped twice round her neck, big as a nest, up to her chin. Almost always has food in one hand (a paper cone of fries, a bun, a peach). Her colour is cherry red.
cast.personality: Worries about nothing. Follows smells, sounds and nice people, falls asleep anywhere, and makes a new friend in every town without trying. Speaks rarely and softly, always sincere, usually about food; her calm solves the problems the others make bigger. Voice: soft, a little husky, slow.

why_clear: Every film is built on ONE big visible thing that changes meaning (in the pilot an orange suitcase: first the problem, then the hero), so the story can be followed by watching that object alone. Each shot shows one action and one reaction face; nothing is implied and nothing has to be remembered from another film. The only text on screen is the spoken line of that shot: three to five everyday words, one line at a time, staying up for the whole shot, never next to a second text. There is no header, no sign, no screen and no narrator. Each line only says what the picture already shows ('It is one night' beside a giant suitcase), so a viewer who reads nothing loses nothing. The three friends are told apart by size and colour before they speak. All films follow the same order: the problem in the first frame, the friend's face, it gets worse, a turn you can see (rain, a door opening, a grandmother walking past), then a hug or a laugh that answers the first frame.
why_young_cool: Three people of 21 to 23 from three countries who speak short simple English because it is their shared second language, exactly like the audience. They tease each other and always end closer; nobody loses and nobody is the fool. Every friend group has a Maya, a Kofi and a Yuki, so viewers tag their own. The look is art-toy figures in streetwear in full sunshine, filmed close like a friend's camera, and the theme is a clap-and-chant track you could sing in a stand. Food and laughter instead of beer and shouting. No brand, no phone, no narrator; one quiet word signs the last second.

episodes.title: One Night
episodes.story: Maya wants to travel light and fast to the match, but Kofi arrives with a giant suitcase for one night and it slows them on every step. Then it rains, the suitcase has a poncho for everyone, and Maya ends up hugging it.

episodes.title: Top Bunk
episodes.story: Maya and Kofi both want the top bunk in the sunny hostel room and race each other up the stairs, squeezing through the door together. Yuki is already asleep in it with her shoes on, so the two rivals tiptoe over and cover her with a blanket.

episodes.title: No Scarf
episodes.story: Maya's rule for the day is no shopping, and she shakes her head at the smiling scarf seller three times. She walks away wearing three new scarves and a hat, prouder than anyone, while Kofi and Yuki follow her grinning.

episodes.title: The Map
episodes.story: Maya leads the way to the stadium with a big paper map, and the crew passes the same sleeping orange cat three times. Yuki sees a grandmother in a football scarf, follows her round one corner, and the stadium lights are right there.

episodes.title: The Chant
episodes.story: In the stand Kofi wants to join the home fans' chant but claps at the wrong moment every time. The old local fan next to him teaches him slowly, clap by clap, and on the sunset train home Kofi is still clapping it while Maya and Yuki sleep on his shoulders.

episodes.title: No Voice
episodes.story: The morning after the match the three want breakfast on a sunny terrace, but nobody has a voice left: only croaks and big gestures come out. The waiter answers with the same croak and points at his own scarf, because he was there too, and all four laugh without a sound.

pilot.title: One Night
pilot.retell: A guy brings a giant suitcase for one night and his friend complains, but when it rains the suitcase has raincoats for everyone and she ends up hugging it.

shots.place: Outside a small train station, late morning, bright sun, peach walls, blue sky.
shots.who: Kofi and Maya
shots.seen: From the first frame an orange suitcase fills the lower half of the picture, with Kofi's big happy face above it and Maya beside it. Kofi rolls the suitcase to a stop next to her with a bump. Maya wears only a tiny white backpack. She looks at the suitcase from bottom to top, then at Kofi. Her eyebrows go up and her mouth falls open.
shots.heard: Maya: "Kofi. It is one night." Suitcase wheels rattling on stone, one heavy bump as it stops. The theme's guitar and shaker start on frame one.
shots.caption: Kofi. It is one night.

shots.place: Same station front, same sun.
shots.who: Kofi
shots.seen: Close on Kofi. He pats the top of the suitcase twice with a flat hand, the way you pat a good dog. He gives a small shrug and a slow, calm smile.
shots.heard: Kofi: "You never know." Two hollow pats on plastic.
shots.caption: You never know.

shots.place: Long stone steps going up between terracotta houses, early afternoon, hard sun and short shadows.
shots.who: Kofi and Maya; Yuki small in the background
shots.seen: The suitcase is stuck halfway up the steps. Kofi pulls the handle from above with both hands, still smiling. Maya pushes from below with both hands and her shoulder, her cheek pressed flat against the orange shell, her feet slipping, her ponytail swinging. The suitcase climbs one step with a bump. At the top of the steps, small in the picture, Yuki sits eating fries and watching, in no hurry.
shots.heard: Maya, out of breath: "What is in here?" Wheels bumping on stone, Maya's breathing.
shots.caption: What is in here?

shots.place: An open square outside the stadium, late afternoon, golden sun with one dark cloud; the stadium is only blurred floodlights and soft shapes of people far behind.
shots.who: Maya, Kofi and Yuki
shots.seen: A big raindrop lands on Maya's nose. All three look up at the sky at the same moment. Rain pours down, shining in the sunlight. Maya pulls her tiny backpack over her head; it covers almost nothing. Yuki bends over her fries to keep them dry. Only Kofi does not hurry: he looks down at his suitcase and smiles.
shots.heard: none. The music drops to one shaker. A roll of thunder, rain hitting the stones, drums from the stadium far away.
shots.caption: none

shots.place: Same square in the sun-shower, low camera at the height of the suitcase.
shots.who: Kofi
shots.seen: The orange suitcase lies flat on the wet stones. Kofi kneels behind it and swings the lid up in one big move. Inside, on top, lie bright yellow rain ponchos folded in a neat row. The yellow shines on his face. He lifts one folded poncho and looks up, past the camera, with a small calm smile.
shots.heard: none. Two clicks of the locks, the lid opening, rain. The guitar riff comes back in.
shots.caption: none

shots.place: Same square, rain falling in golden light.
shots.who: Yuki and Kofi
shots.seen: Yuki and Kofi stand side by side in bright yellow ponchos with the hoods up, dry and happy; the brim of Yuki's red hat sticks out under her hood. Yuki holds her paper cone of fries and looks up at Kofi. Kofi, looking straight ahead, lifts a red sauce bottle up into the picture in his own fist. Yuki's eyes go wide and she leans her head against his arm.
shots.heard: Yuki: "Do you have ketchup?" Rain tapping on the plastic hoods. One short brass stab as the bottle comes up.
shots.caption: Do you have ketchup?

shots.place: Same square, the rain thinning, the sun breaking through, floodlights glowing behind.
shots.who: Maya in front; Kofi and Yuki behind her, slightly soft
shots.seen: Maya, in a yellow poncho with the hood pushed back so her ponytail shows, has both arms wrapped round the standing orange suitcase. Her cheek rests on top of it, eyes closed, smiling. She opens her eyes, looks up at Kofi and speaks, still hugging it. Behind her Kofi laughs with his whole body and Yuki grins. Maya squeezes the suitcase tighter. The last frame, Maya's happy face against the suitcase, answers the first frame, her shocked face beside it.
shots.heard: Maya: "Next time, bring two." Kofi's big laugh, not cut clean. The full theme with the group 'oh-oh' voices and claps; singing and drums from the stadium rising.
shots.caption: Next time, bring two.

pilot.end_card: About 2 seconds on a plain cream background: the word VENUVOY in the middle, the pink-and-yellow crew scarf lying under it like an underline, and one small line below: "See you on the next trip." Sound: the last clap-clap and the group 'oh-oh'. No logo animation, no app, no link.

risks: Voices change between shots or films (it happened in the first series). Plan: one locked voice reference per character, used for every line in every film; lines are 3 to 5 words with one speaker per shot. Plan B: replace all dialogue in the edit with the locked voice, or play the line over the listener's face with the caption carrying it. The film works with no lines at all.

Lip-sync looks wrong on stylised faces. Plan: test one 4-second speaking clip per character before generating any film. Plan B: frame the speaker from behind or with the poncho hood hiding the mouth and cut to the reaction face.

A character drifts (face, hair, clothes). Plan: one reference sheet and one outfit per person for ever, three very different sizes and one owned colour each; every clip starts from a designed still that is checked against the sheet before any video is made. Plan B: if a three-person still fails (shots 4 and 7), split it into single faces cut on the beat.

The suitcase changes size, colour or shape between shots (the 'cup that changed hands' kind of slip). Plan: the suitcase gets its own reference sheet like a cast member: tangerine orange, chest-high on Maya, scarf on the handle. Nothing is passed hand to hand anywhere in the script: the ponchos are never handed over on camera (cut from the open suitcase to people already wearing them) and the ketchup comes up in Kofi's own fist.

Opening the suitcase needs precise hands. Plan: the still starts with the lid already a hand's width open and Kofi only swings it up. Plan B: start with the lid fully open and Kofi simply raising his head with the poncho, or drop shot 5 and show the open suitcase in the foreground of shot 6.

Generated rain turns the picture grey or looks fake. Plan: a sun-shower, with the golden backlight kept and rain as bright chunky streaks in the same style. Plan B: generate the clips dry from wet-looking stills and add rain streaks and splashes in the edit.
The ketchup beat confuses or the bottle morphs. It is removable: without it shot 6 is simply Yuki and Kofi dry and happy in ponchos, and the film is still complete at about 25 seconds.

The closing line fails and has to be patched (as last time). Plan: generate shot 7 first, before anything else, as the make-or-break clip: four words, one speaker, mouth clearly visible. Plan B: end on the silent hug of the suitcase with Kofi's laugh; the picture alone pays off the first shot.

The stylised look reads as a children's cartoon. Plan: adult proportions, streetwear, real fabric textures, handheld camera, natural sound and the dance theme; approve one line-up still of the three friends with the client before any video. Plan B: push the design further toward art-toy and stop-motion (matte clay, motion held at 12 pictures a second in the edit), which also hides wobble in generated movement.

Garbled text, sharp crowds or a black band in the frame. Plan: the world has no letters by design, the stadium is only light and sound, crowds stay as soft colour shapes, and every still is made full-frame 9:16 and checked for bands before video. The suitcase never enters a stadium, so fans cannot say 'that would not be allowed in'.
Viewers feel tricked by AI. Plan: the look never pretends to be real people and every film is posted with the platform's AI-generated label switched on.

title: First Away
premise: Three friends go on their first football trip abroad, and each film is one small mission on the way to the match (catch the train, find the hostel, get the scarf, find the stadium, learn the song, reach the seat) that ends warm.
look:
STYLISED, not photoreal: a warm handmade stop-motion look. Characters look like hand-sculpted matte clay figures (soft thumbprint texture, slightly big heads, chunky simple hands, big eyes and eyebrows, mouths that open wide). Clothes are felt and knitted wool with visible fibres. Sets look like painted miniature models. Never glossy plastic, never flat vector art.
PALETTE: the world is cream, peach-pink, sky blue and leaf green. Strong colours belong only to the cast, one each: Nina tangerine, Otto cobalt blue with a sunflower-yellow suitcase, Sami mint green. The team colours are an invented pair, tangerine and violet stripes, so a scarf is spotted at once and matches no real club.
LIGHT: sun only. The season is one day, from sunrise gold in film 1 to golden hour at kick-off in film 6. Hard warm sun, soft blue shadows. Every interior has a big window with sun in it. No night, no dim room, no grey grade.
LENS: as if a friend films on a small handheld camera at eye level. Wide (24 to 28 mm feel), close to faces, a light handheld bob, the camera moves with the people. Shallow miniature depth of field, so backgrounds, signs and crowds melt into soft colour shapes.
FINISH: native 9:16, conformed in the edit to 12 frames per second for the stop-motion feel, with light grain.
WARDROBE: one locked outfit per character in block colours, no words, no badges.
WORLD: an invented sunny town in no real country: pastel houses, tiled lanes, a blue fountain, a tram, plane trees. The stadium is only floodlights, sound and a blur of green.
WHY: (1) clay figures forgive what generated video does badly (hands, small face drift, floaty movement), and the 12 fps finish hides wobble; (2) it does not pretend to be real people, which is the honest and safer way to use AI with this age group; (3) colour-coded chunky figures read on a phone with the sound off; (4) it is the opposite of the first series in every signal: sunny, handmade, colourful, young.
music: One theme made for the series, called "First Away": warm afro-house with an amapiano log-drum bounce, 120 bpm, major key. Instruments: hand claps in a stadium pattern (clap-clap, clap-clap-clap), shakers, light congas, log-drum bass, one bright palm-muted guitar riff you can hum, a small brass stab on payoffs, and a group "oh-oh-oh" sung by a few young voices as if in a stand. No whistling, no ukulele, no trailer drums. Shape in every film: the claps start on the first frame, the guitar riff runs under the obstacle, the "oh-oh-oh" lands exactly on the payoff shot, and two last claps close the end card. At 120 bpm a beat is half a second, so every cut lands on a beat. The clap pattern is also the song the locals teach in film 5. Natural sound sits loud on top: suitcase wheels on stone, station echo, uncut laughter, a muffled roar. Feeling: sun on your face, running with your friends, something good is about to start.

cast.name: Nina
cast.look: Small and quick, about 158 cm, compact sporty build. Warm dark-brown skin, round face, big dark-brown eyes, strong arched eyebrows, a wide smile with a small gap between the front teeth. Black curly hair in two high round puffs tied with tangerine bands. Always the same clothes: a tangerine-orange short-sleeved football shirt with a violet collar and violet sleeve cuffs (plain, no badge, no words), an open light-blue denim jacket with the sleeves rolled to the elbow, loose cream cargo trousers, chunky white trainers, a small violet backpack on both shoulders. Her colour is tangerine.
cast.personality: Has waited her whole life for this match. Always moving forward: walks backwards to hurry the others, bounces on her toes when she has to wait. Never angry; when something goes wrong her eyebrows jump, she gets an idea and gets faster. Hugs first, asks later. Voice: bright, quick, a little husky.

cast.name: Otto
cast.look: Very tall and thin, about 193 cm, long arms and legs, shoulders a little stooped, bends down to talk to people. Pale skin with freckles over the nose and cheeks, long face, big ears, soft light-green eyes, a gentle half smile. Thick wavy copper-red hair falling over the forehead. Always the same clothes: a cobalt-blue zip hoodie one size too big over a plain white T-shirt, knee-length sand-coloured shorts, white socks pulled up, moss-green trainers. On travel films he pulls a giant sunflower-yellow hard suitcase: rounded corners, hip-high on him (about one metre), four small black wheels, black handle, no stickers, no strap. In town (films 3 to 6) he wears a small backpack in the same yellow. His colours are cobalt and yellow.
cast.personality: A gentle giant who packs for every possible problem and is proud of it. Careful and kind, says sorry to a door he bumps into. Slow to start, but once he is in, he is the loudest and happiest of the three. Treats the yellow suitcase like a pet. Voice: soft, low, slow.

cast.name: Sami
cast.look: Medium height, about 175 cm, soft round build, slow relaxed walk. Light olive-brown skin, round cheeks, heavy sleepy eyelids always half closed, thick straight black eyebrows, a small calm smile. Short black hair, mostly hidden because the hood is always up. Always the same clothes: a mint-green hoodie two sizes too big with the hood up and sleeves that cover his hands, wide grey jogging trousers, black-and-white trainers. Always hugging a worn classic football (white with black patches) under his left arm; it is also his pillow. His colour is mint.
cast.personality: Can sleep anywhere: standing, walking, on a suitcase. Worries about nothing and says almost nothing. In each film he wakes for one perfect moment, does or says one small right thing, and goes back to sleep. Voice: a slow sleepy mumble.

why_clear: Each film has one goal you can SEE (a train, a door, a scarf, floodlights, a clap, the top of the stairs), and the single top line names it in a few plain words ("Mission 1: catch the train"). That line stays on screen for the whole film, so nobody has to read fast. The obstacle is always a physical thing in the frame (a suitcase too heavy to run with, the same fountain passed three times, an empty scarf rail, two arms pointing opposite ways, a clap one beat late, stairs that never end). The payoff is always an action, never a line or a caption (they roll onto the train, a girl leads them to the door, a scarf goes round a neck, they turn and follow the scarves, he claps in time, the pitch opens). Each friend is one block colour and one trait shown by action (running, dragging the giant suitcase, asleep), so a viewer knows who is who in two seconds without names. Nothing inside the picture has to be read: no chat, no signs, no screens. Spoken lines are two to four everyday words and only repeat what the picture already shows; captions are big, sentence case, one short line at a time in the lower middle, on screen at least a second and a half. No film needs another film: the mission number is only a label, and every film starts with the problem in the first second and ends finished.
why_young_cool: It is three friends in their early twenties you would want to travel with, in full sun, moving all the time, on a beat you would put in a playlist. The handmade clay look feels made by people and not by a brand studio, and it is honest about being animation. The mission frame is the language of games: a clear goal, a small win, a good feeling at the end. The humour is in situations and faces and it is always kind: the friend who packs too much turns out to be the hero, the sleepy friend wakes at exactly the right moment, and the locals are the generous ones (the guard waves them in, a girl shows the way, an old fan gives away his scarf, a drummer teaches the song). Everyone knows these three types in their own group, so people tag the friend who is Otto or Sami. There is no app, no phone screen, no price and no slogan; the brand signs for one second. The season ends where the match begins, so the feeling left is "I want that trip with my friends".

episodes.title: Mission 1: Catch the train
episodes.story: The three must catch the morning train, but Otto's giant suitcase is too heavy to run with and Sami is asleep on his feet. Nina sits Sami on the suitcase, they push it like a race cart to the door, and the suitcase becomes their seat on the train.

episodes.title: Mission 2: Find the hostel
episodes.story: They want to leave the giant suitcase at the hostel, but every sunny lane looks the same and they pass the same blue fountain three times. Sami's football rolls away to a local girl, who kicks it back, waves "follow me" and runs them to the right door, where her grandmother meets them with open arms.

episodes.title: Mission 3: Get the scarf
episodes.story: Nina wants her first team scarf, but the seller's rail is empty: she is one minute too late. An old local fan on a bench sees her face, takes off his own faded scarf and puts it round her neck; she hugs him and walks away holding it high.

episodes.title: Mission 4: Find the stadium
episodes.story: Nina points left, Otto points right, and they turn the paper map round and round. Sami wakes and turns them both by the shoulders: behind them a river of orange-and-violet scarves is walking one way, so they follow it round one corner and the floodlights stand over the roofs.

episodes.title: Mission 5: Learn the song
episodes.story: Outside the ground the local fans clap their song and Otto claps one beat late every time. A local drummer his age slows the beat just for him, clap by clap, until he has it, and he ends as the loudest of all with the locals cheering him.

episodes.title: Mission 6: Reach the seat
episodes.story: Their seats are in the top row and the stairs never end: legs shake, Sami falls asleep on a step, Nina and Otto pull him up by the sleeves. On the last step the light and the roar open in front of them, the green pitch shines below, and for the first time Sami's eyes are wide open.

pilot.title: Mission 1: Catch the train
pilot.header: First football trip. Mission 1: catch the train.
pilot.retell: They almost missed the train because of the giant suitcase, so they put their sleepy friend on it, pushed it like a race cart and made it.

shots.place: Big station hall, early morning. Low golden sun through tall windows, long shadows on a pale stone floor.
shots.who: Nina close and sharp; Otto with the giant yellow suitcase far behind her, soft.
shots.seen: The camera runs backwards in front of Nina. Her face fills the frame: wide eyes, mouth open, sprinting. She looks back over her shoulder and waves her whole arm: come on. Far behind her, tall Otto drags a yellow suitcase as big as a fridge and is falling behind.
shots.heard: Nina: "Otto! Run! The train!" Fast footsteps, suitcase wheels rumbling on stone, station echo. The theme starts with claps on the first frame.
shots.caption: Otto! Run! The train!

shots.place: The platform, open air, bright morning sun.
shots.who: The guard: a local woman of about fifty, round kind face, navy uniform and cap, beside a chunky cream-and-red train.
shots.seen: The train waits with one door open. The guard stands next to the door and looks at her wrist. Then she looks up along the platform, straight at us, and lifts one arm high. A whistle hangs from her other hand.
shots.heard: none. One short whistle, the train humming.
shots.caption: none

shots.place: Station hall, same golden light.
shots.who: Otto and Sami with the yellow suitcase.
shots.seen: Otto pulls the suitcase with both hands, leaning far forward, red in the face. The suitcase hardly moves. Beside it Sami walks with his eyes closed, hood up, football under his arm, one sleeve resting on the suitcase: asleep on his feet. Otto stops, bends over with his hands on his knees and shakes his head.
shots.heard: Otto: "It is too heavy!" Hard breathing, the wheels squeak to a stop.
shots.caption: It is too heavy!

shots.place: Station hall, same spot.
shots.who: Nina and Sami, with the top of the suitcase between them.
shots.seen: Nina runs back into the frame and stops. She looks at the suitcase. She looks at sleeping Sami. Her eyebrows jump up and a big grin spreads over her face. She slaps the top of the suitcase twice with a flat hand.
shots.heard: Nina: "I have an idea!" Two slaps on the suitcase, in time with the claps in the music.
shots.caption: I have an idea!

shots.place: Station hall towards the platform. Sunbeams and pillars fly past.
shots.who: Sami on top of the suitcase in front; Nina and Otto pushing behind him.
shots.seen: The camera is low in front and flies backwards. Sami sits on top of the yellow suitcase, slumped forward, fast asleep, hugging the football, smiling in his sleep. Right behind him Nina and Otto push the suitcase side by side at full sprint, cheeks puffed, hair flying. They start to laugh.
shots.heard: none. Wheels roaring on stone, Nina and Otto laughing, the group "oh-oh-oh" of the theme.
shots.caption: none

shots.place: The platform at the open train door, bright sun.
shots.who: The guard close; the three friends pass as a yellow, orange and blue blur.
shots.seen: The guard sees them coming. Her eyebrows shoot up, then she laughs, steps to the side and sweeps her arm towards the open door. The yellow suitcase with sleeping Sami on top and the two pushers shoots past her and in through the door.
shots.heard: Guard: "Quick! Quick!" Wheels, one door beep.
shots.caption: Quick! Quick!

shots.place: Inside the train by a big window. Bright sun; green fields start to slide past.
shots.who: Nina, Sami and Otto sitting in a row on the yellow suitcase, which lies on its side like a bench.
shots.seen: The three sit side by side on the suitcase: Nina, Sami in the middle, Otto. Nina and Otto are out of breath. They look at each other and burst out laughing, and Otto pats the suitcase like a good dog. Sami opens one eye, looks left and right and says something. Then his head drops on Otto's shoulder and he sleeps again. Nina throws both fists in the air.
shots.heard: Sami: "Are we there?" Train wheels, laughter that is not cut clean. The theme lands its last claps.
shots.caption: Are we there?

pilot.end_card: VENUVOY, alone on a sunny cream card for 2 seconds, with one small line under it: "See you at the match." The last two claps of the theme. Total film: 28 seconds of shots plus the 2-second card = 30 seconds.

risks: Faces, clothes or props drift between shots and films. Plan: one locked outfit and one block colour per character, a reference sheet for each (front, three-quarter, side, full body, six expressions) plus one for the yellow suitcase and one for the football; make ALL seven start stills first, look at them side by side and approve them before any video is made. Plan B: recolour or repaint the still, never fix it in the video.

Shot 5 (Sami riding the suitcase while two people push) is the hardest clip: three figures, wheels, speed. Plan B: frame tighter so the wheels are out of the picture (Sami's sleeping face in front, the two pushing faces behind, background streaking); or split it into two simple clips (Sami alone gliding asleep on the suitcase, then Nina and Otto pushing) and merge shots 3 and 4 into one to stay at seven shots.

Train doors and the moment of rolling in (shot 6) can come out wrong, and four figures in one frame is a lot. Plan B: the guard alone, close, reacting and sweeping her arm while the wheels and the door beep are only heard; cut straight to the inside of the train. Doors are never shown moving.
The guard's whistle and wrist are small hand details. Plan B: she only raises one arm and smiles; the whistle is a sound.

Readable text sneaks into the picture (station signs, a clock, the train's front). Plan: design the stills with blank shapes for signs and keep the background soft; paint out anything letter-like in the still before it is animated. A clip with garbled letters is rejected, not patched.

The clay look comes out as glossy plastic or changes material from shot to shot. Plan: one approved style frame and a short material list (matte clay skin with thumbprints, felt clothes, painted model sets) reused word for word in every prompt. Plan B: a simpler smooth matte toy look used everywhere; the 12 fps finish and light grain in the edit pull the shots together.

Lip-sync on clay faces looks off, or a voice changes between films. Plan: every line is two to four words, one speaker per shot, one fixed voice per character chosen once and reused. Plan B: put the line over the back of the speaker's head or drop it; the film is written to work with no words at all.

Production slips like last time (a black band, a prop that moves, a patched ending). Plan: generate in native 9:16 and check every clip for bands; nobody hands anything to anybody in this film; the football is always under Sami's left arm and the suitcase is always plain yellow; the ending is one single clip with one short line, so nothing has to be patched from another take.

The header and the captions fight for the eye. Plan: the header sits small at the top for the whole film; captions appear one at a time in the lower middle for at least a second and a half; never two texts arriving at once. Plan B: drop the caption of shot 6 ("Quick! Quick!"), since the gesture says it.

A mission number may make a new viewer think an earlier film is needed. Plan B: remove the number from the header ("First football trip. Mission: catch the train.") and keep the number only in the post text.

The three-person final shot loses a face. Plan B: a two-shot of Nina and Otto laughing on the suitcase with Sami's mint hood resting on Otto's shoulder at the edge of the frame; his line is heard from under the hood.

The generated theme sounds like stock music, or the sung hook sounds artificial. Plan B: keep only claps, drums, bass and the guitar riff, and record the "oh-oh-oh" as a simple group shout; the cuts stay on the beat either way.
The films are AI-made animation. Post them with the platform's AI label switched on; the look never pretends to be real people.

title: Trip Trip Hooray
premise: Three friends in their early twenties travel abroad for a football match, and in every film one small trip problem is met and solved without a single spoken word: only faces, action and a beat you can clap.
look:
STYLISED, not photoreal: a handmade miniature world filmed as if a friend were holding the camera.

Characters: clay-and-fabric puppets of young adults (long legs, trainers, streetwear; not babies, not toys). Matte clay skin with a soft thumbprint texture, big round eyes, thick eyebrows that do the acting, simple chunky four-finger hands, real-looking knitted scarves and nylon jackets. Movement is smooth, not jerky.

World: one invented sunny hill town by the sea, built like a model: pastel plaster houses (peach, butter yellow, pale mint), terracotta roofs, stone steps, washing lines, lemon trees in pots. It is a world without letters: signs are plain colours and simple pictures. The stadium is never shown: only four floodlight masts over the roofs, a glow and a roar. Crowds are soft out-of-focus shapes with scarves. One small local runs through the films: a fat orange street cat.

Palette: toy-bright colour in warm sun. Each friend owns one colour (Lola sunflower yellow, Timo cobalt blue with the hot-pink suitcase, Yuki cream with lime green). The friends' trip scarf is wide hot-pink and turquoise stripes with a white fringe; home fans wear plain orange scarves with violet ends. No words or badges on anything.

Light: always day. Low golden morning sun or late-afternoon sun, hard warm light, long soft shadows, blue sky; even the rain falls through sunshine. No night, no grey, no dim rooms.

Lens: eye level, close to faces, gently handheld, slightly imperfect framing, macro-style shallow focus that melts backgrounds into colour, one simple move per shot. Frames are stacked for vertical 9:16 (umbrella at the top, faces in the middle, suitcase at the bottom), with the top 15 percent kept free for the one top line.

Wardrobe: one locked outfit per friend in every film.

Why: silent comedy needs big readable faces, and a dropped jaw is charming on a puppet where it looks overacted on a realistic face. The look openly says "made by hand" and does not pretend to be real people. It hides the weak spots of generated video: no lip-sync because nobody speaks, mitten-like hands, no readable text, soft crowds. And every signal is the opposite of the first series: sunny, colourful, playful, young.
music:
One original theme shared by all films, "the clap theme", at 122 beats per minute: warm, percussive dance music. Soft four-on-the-floor kick, a bouncing log-drum bass, shaker, a bright nylon-string guitar riff, trumpet and trombone stabs, and two hooks anybody can copy: a handclap pattern (clap-clap, clap-clap-clap) and a four-note group "oh-oh-oh-oh" sung by a few young mixed voices, like a small stand.

Shape in every film: it starts on the first frame with claps and guitar, grows through the obstacles, stops dead for about one second on "the Look" (only natural sound), and comes back at full with brass and the group voices on the payoff. It ends on two claps so the film loops. Actions land on the beat (the suitcase bumps on the steps, Timo's two pats).

Feeling: sunny, bouncing, a little cheeky, friendly; a track for a playlist, not stock music. No ukulele, no whistling, no trailer drums.

Natural sound is mixed loud: wheels on stone, rain on fabric, the muffled roar through the streets. The friends have voices but no words: gasps, laughs, hums, cheers, all added in the sound mix.

cast.name: Lola
cast.look: Small and springy, about 1.60 m, light athletic build, always on her toes. Dark-brown skin, heart-shaped face, very big dark eyes, strong straight eyebrows (the left one lifts on its own), a wide grin with a small gap between her front teeth. Black hair in two big round puffs high on her head, like two pom-poms, each held by a turquoise band; small gold hoop earrings. Always: sunflower-yellow windbreaker with the sleeves pushed up, white T-shirt, wide cream cargo trousers, white chunky trainers with pink laces, a tiny turquoise backpack, and the trip scarf (wide hot-pink and turquoise stripes, white fringe, no words, no badge) tied once round her neck with the ends flying.
cast.personality: The engine. Awake first, dressed first, at the door first. She bounces, points the way, counts her friends and pulls them along. Her impatience lasts two seconds: one raised eyebrow (the Look), then a grin she cannot hold back and a hug that nearly knocks people over.

cast.name: Timo
cast.look: Very tall, about 1.95 m, big and soft, round shoulders, a small belly, big slow hands. Pale skin, pink cheeks and a nose that is always a little sunburned. Straw-blond hair in a fluffy mop that falls over his forehead, small kind light-blue eyes under pale eyebrows, a slow closed smile that goes up more on the right. Always: cobalt-blue fleece zipped to the chin, sand-coloured cargo trousers, grey walking shoes, the trip scarf hanging long and open, never tied. Always with him: a hot-pink hard suitcase on four wheels, as tall as Lola's shoulder and as wide as a door, with a turquoise strap round its middle.
cast.personality: The calm one. Never hurries, never worries, and has packed for every possible problem. When things go wrong he looks at it, smiles, pats his suitcase twice and fixes it. He shares whatever he has with anyone standing near, so locals like him at once.

cast.name: Yuki
cast.look: Medium-small, about 1.65 m, slim, soft posture, always leaning on something or somebody. Light skin, East Asian features, small round face, straight black hair in a blunt chin-length bob with a heavy fringe, a tiny beauty mark under her right eye. Heavy-lidded dark eyes, half closed by default, huge and shining when she is awake. Always: a cream oversized teddy fleece down to mid-thigh with sleeves that cover her hands, loose charcoal trousers, lime-green trainers, a lime-green travel pillow round her neck with the trip scarf tucked under it, and a lime-green sleep mask pushed up into her fringe.
cast.personality: The sleeper. She can sleep standing, walking, in a queue, in the rain, and nothing bothers her. She wakes at exactly the right second and is then the loudest fan of all. Lucky without trying.

why_clear:
Nobody speaks, so there is nothing to translate and nothing is lost with the sound off. Each film follows the same five rules.

1. The problem is in the picture in the first second (a tiny backpack next to a suitcase as big as a door).
2. Cause and effect are physical and in order: stairs make them slow, rain makes them wet, the umbrella makes them dry, she hugs the bag.
3. The three friends are readable by shape and colour with no labels: the small yellow one who runs ahead, the giant blue one with the giant pink suitcase, the one in the blanket-fleece with the travel pillow who is asleep.
4. Every sound that matters is doubled by a picture: the stadium roar is always seen as something shaking (an umbrella, food on a tray, pigeons flying up, every head lifting), and the music stop is always a held look between two faces.
5. The payoff is an action in the last seconds, never a line, a caption or the end card, and it turns the first picture upside down (horror at the bag becomes a hug for the bag).

Each shot holds one idea for three to six seconds in close, sunny frames. The only words on screen are one plain "When..." line that stays up for the first twelve seconds, and the brand at the end. The six lines are: When your friend packs for one night. When your friends will not wake up. When your friend can sleep anywhere. When you say you will not buy a scarf. When you do not know the clap. When you always miss the goal. No film needs another film; the same three friends are the only thread.
why_young_cool:
Three friends in their early twenties whom everybody already has in their own group: the one who is always first, the one with the giant bag, the one who sleeps anywhere. That is the reason to tag a friend and share.

The picture is sun, colour and streetwear in a handmade world that looks like nothing else in the feed and does not fake real people. The track is a dance beat you would add to a playlist, with a clap you can do in a stand; cuts land on the beat and the film loops.

The humour is warm: the friend who causes the problem is the hero by the end, nobody is the fool, and the locals (a scarf seller, a kid with a drum, a food seller, a street cat) are generous and cool. Women are at the centre as fans.
