look:
STYLISED, not photoreal: collectible art-toy figures in streetwear, filmed on a hand-built miniature town in real sunlight. Not clay puppets, not a baby cartoon, not glossy studio 3D and not flat vector art.

FIGURES: adult proportions (long legs, head about one sixth of the height). Matte skin with a soft handmade surface. Eyes and eyebrows big enough to read on a phone, but smaller than cartoon eyes. Simple chunky hands. Hair sculpted as one solid shape that never turns into strands; in wind only scarves and shirts move. Clothes look like real fabric at toy scale, with a coarse soft weave (no fine pattern that can shimmer). Lived-in, not new: scuffed trainers, a creased shirt, loose laces.

WORLD: one invented sunny hill town used for every trip, built like a model. Painted houses in cream, terracotta, mint and sky blue, cobbled streets, low walls, plain bunting. No letters, numbers or clocks anywhere; signs are colour shapes or simple pictures. The stadium is only ever a soft cream bowl with four floodlight masts and plain flags, plus its sound. Other fans are still, soft colour shapes holding scarves up. Near every ground stands the bag hut, a small striped hut with shelves of bags, where Big Yellow waits during a match. One recurring local: the fat ginger cat.

PALETTE: cream base. Teal belongs to Timo, coral belongs to Luna, sunflower yellow is what they share (her suitcase, his watch, her socks). The trip scarf carries both friends: one half teal, one half coral, cream fringe; it belongs to no club. The home colours of the town are cream and violet. The darkest colour is deep violet; no black and no grey; shadows are warm.

LIGHT: always sun. The standard is low golden late afternoon; mornings are pink-gold; interiors are flooded from a big window; rain exists only as a sun-shower. The sun is always low on screen left and a little in front of the faces, in every shot: geography is cheated, faces never are.

LENS AND FRAME: as if a third friend is filming: eye level, close to faces, soft macro background. Clips are generated with a still or very simple camera, and the small hand wobble is added in the edit. Full-frame 9:16. The screen grammar never changes: Luna on the left, Timo on the right, faces in the upper half, the caption band below them.

FINISH: a warm grade checked against three fixed swatches (teal, coral, yellow) and against Timo's skin tone, with light grain. The stop-motion step (12 pictures a second) is used only if it passes a test on the ride clip and on one speaking clip; otherwise every film stays smooth. The two are never mixed.

WARDROBE: one locked outfit per friend in every film, with no one-sided details (nothing that exists on only the left or the right, except the watch on Timo's left wrist).

WHY THIS LOOK: (1) It is honest: it does not pretend generated people are real, which this age group rejects. (2) Riding a suitcase down a hill is charming for a toy figure and a dangerous stunt for a real person. (3) It hides the weak spots of generated video: simple hands, no text, soft crowds, and characters that stay the same because they are strong shapes in fixed colours. (4) Two colours and two heights tell a twelve-year-old who is who with the sound off. (5) At one glance it is the opposite of the first series: sun, colour and play instead of night, grey and seriousness. The art-toy finish (long legs, small eyes, real streetwear) is what keeps it from reading as a children's programme.
music:
One theme made for the series, working name "Tick Tock Clap": sunny afro-house with an amapiano bounce at exactly 120 beats a minute, in a major key, built and delivered in separate layers so that the edit can drop layers in and out. At 120 every shot length in the scripts is a whole number of beats and the two-second end card is exactly four beats.

TWO MOTIFS: Timo is a tidy tick-tock on woodblock and muted marimba, exactly on the beat. Luna is a lazy log-drum bass with a cowbell that lands a little late. When the two friends agree, both motifs lock together under a five-clap stand pattern (clap, clap, clap-clap-clap) and a three-note "oh-oh-oh" sung by three or four young mixed voices, rough and slightly out of tune, like friends in a stand. No words, and it must not resemble any real club chant.

CHARACTER: drums and shaker lead, not guitar. It has to knock on a phone speaker, so the tick-tock and the claps carry the track when the bass disappears. The voices are used only on the payoff. No whistling, no ukulele, no trailer drums, no whoosh effects, no trending sound.

SHAPE IN EVERY FILM: tick-tock and shaker from frame one with no intro; the log drum joins when the problem gets worse; everything thins at the offer and drops to the tick-tock alone on the "No"; the full groove lands on the hard cut; the "oh-oh-oh" and the claps land on the turn; one breath of near silence on the topper; then the hook runs to the last three claps on the card. The last clap ends dry so the loop does not click.

SOUND: natural sound is mixed as loud as the music (wheels on cobbles, puffing, wind, a far crowd, a laugh that is not cut clean). Stadium drums in the natural sound are played in the theme's tempo. All human sounds come from the two locked voices. Any music the generated clips produce by themselves is removed.

FEELING: walking to the ground with your best friend on a warm evening.

episodes.title: One Night (pilot)
episodes.story: Timo wants to walk light and fast to the match, but Luna has brought a giant suitcase for one night, and pushing it up the hill is so slow that a cat overtakes them. At the top she sits on it, he says no, and one cut later they ride it down to the stadium, shoot past the cat, and he hugs the suitcase.

episodes.title: Wake Up, Luna
episodes.story: At sunrise Timo is dressed with his scarf on and wants the early train, but Luna pulls the blanket back over her head and says no. One cut later she is walking down the sunny street with her eyes shut, wrapped in the blanket, following the warm pastry Timo holds in front of her nose; on the train she is wide awake and eating it, and he is the one asleep.

episodes.title: Try It
episodes.story: Timo wants to eat the neat sandwiches he packed, while Luna holds a huge steaming flatbread from a street stand under his nose and he shakes his head. One cut later he has a flatbread in each hand and sauce on his chin, and Luna is happily eating his sandwiches.

episodes.title: Just In Case
episodes.story: Under a blue sky Timo packs two rain ponchos into his tiny backpack, and Luna laughs, points at the sun and says no. One cut later a sun-shower is pouring, both are in ponchos with the hoods up, dancing to the stadium, and Luna hugs his tiny backpack.

episodes.title: No Scarf
episodes.story: Timo's rule for the day is no shopping, so he shakes his head at the smiling scarf seller, who only holds a scarf a little higher each time he looks back. One cut later he walks away in three scarves, a hat and a flag as a cape, prouder than anyone, with Luna grinning beside him and the seller waving.

episodes.title: The Clap
episodes.story: By a sunny wall outside the gate Luna joins the home fans' clap loudly and wrongly, her hands meeting exactly when the others are apart, while Timo knows it but claps tiny and shy. A local fan their age offers to show her, she says no, she knows it, and one cut later he is teaching her clap by clap with big slow arms until all three clap over their heads together.

episodes.title: Top Row
episodes.story: Their seats are in the top row and the sunny stairway never ends, so Luna sits down on a step and says no more stairs. Then paper streamers drift down from the light at the top; one cut later she is running up two steps at a time, and on the last step green and gold light falls on both faces: Luna stops chewing, Timo forgets his watch, and they just stand and look.

episodes.title: No Voice
episodes.story: After two seconds of both roaring at a goal, it is the next morning on a sunny terrace: they want breakfast, but nothing comes out of their mouths and both hands go to their throats. Timo crosses his arms and refuses to mime; one cut later both are acting out the order with their whole bodies, and the waiter answers with the same hand on his throat and points at his own scarf, because he was there too.

pilot.title: One Night
pilot.retell: His friend brought a giant suitcase for one night, and pushing it up the hill was so slow that a cat overtook them, so they rode it down the other side to the stadium, shot past the cat, and he ended up hugging the suitcase.

shots.place: A small square outside a train station in the invented football town: a plain cream arch with a soft cream-and-teal train carriage standing behind it. Late afternoon, low golden sun from the left, cobbles, plain bunting overhead. Behind Timo a street climbs steeply; over its top stand four floodlight masts.
shots.who: Luna and Timo
shots.seen: From the first frame a yellow suitcase as big as a washing machine stands in the middle of the picture. It rocks once on its wheels and stands still. On the left stands Luna, short, in a coral football shirt, one hand flat on the suitcase, smiling proudly with her mouth closed. On the right, close to the camera, stands Timo, tall, in a teal jacket, one thumb under the strap of a tiny backpack, his other arm stretched out and pointing up the steep street to four floodlight masts. Both wear the same teal-and-coral scarf. Timo's eyes travel from the bottom of the suitcase up to its top. His pointing arm slowly sinks. His mouth falls open and he speaks to Luna.
shots.heard: Timo: "Luna. It's one night!" Natural sound: a last rattle of small wheels on stone and one heavy bump, the hum of the train, a crowd far away. Music: the tick-tock and shaker start on frame one.
shots.caption: Luna. It's one night!

shots.place: A steep cobbled street between painted houses, seen from the side: it climbs from right to left. Same golden sun. A garden wall runs along the far side, its top higher than everyone's heads. Over the top of the street, the four floodlight masts, bigger now.
shots.who: Luna, Timo and the ginger cat
shots.seen: The yellow suitcase is stuck halfway up the steep street and hardly moves. We see the friends from the knees up. On the left, above the suitcase, Luna leans back as in a tug-of-war, both hands on its handle, cheeks puffed out. On the right, below it, Timo pushes with both hands and one shoulder, his cheek squashed flat against the yellow shell, his face towards us. On top of the wall behind them a fat ginger cat strolls up the hill. It passes Timo, passes the suitcase, passes Luna. Timo's eyes follow the cat; his head does not move. Ahead of them the cat stops and looks back at them once.
shots.heard: none (no words). Natural sound: small wheels grinding slowly on cobbles, both friends puffing, trainers slipping, one small "mrrp" from the cat. Music: the lazy log drum comes in.
shots.caption: none

shots.place: The top of the hill, same golden sun. On the far side the street falls away, long and straight, with roofs stepping down, to the stadium below: a round cream bowl with four lit floodlight masts and flags, bright in the sun, with small still shapes of fans around it.
shots.who: Luna and Timo
shots.seen: The stadium lies below them at the bottom of a long straight street; we see it in the gap between the two friends. On the left the suitcase stands on the last flat stones before the slope, and Luna is already sitting on the front half of its lid, turned towards Timo, feet off the ground, with a huge grin. One of her arms points straight down the hill at the stadium. With her other hand she pats the empty half of the lid behind her, twice. On the right Timo stands with both palms up. He shakes his head, says no, and takes one step back.
shots.heard: Timo: "No. No, no, no." Natural sound: two hollow pats on the lid, a far crowd and drums rising from below, one squeak of a wheel, Luna's giggle. Music: thins to bass and shaker, then drops to the tick-tock alone on the "No".
shots.caption: No. No, no, no.

shots.place: The long downhill street, sun flashing between the houses; the walls on both sides are soft bands of colour.
shots.who: Luna and Timo, both sitting on the suitcase
shots.seen: Hard cut. Both are riding the suitcase down the hill, straight towards the camera, which flies backwards just ahead of them. We see them from the chest up; the yellow lid is a wide bar across the bottom of the picture. Luna sits in front with both arms up in a wide V and her mouth wide open in a laugh. Timo sits behind her, his face in the gap above her head: eyes huge, mouth wide open in a scream, both hands clamped on her shoulders. Scarves and shirts flap. The street behind them streaks past.
shots.heard: none (no words). Natural sound: Timo's long scream, Luna's whoop, wheels roaring on cobbles, wind. Music: the full groove lands exactly on the cut.
shots.caption: none

shots.place: The same downhill street, further down, same sun.
shots.who: Luna and Timo, both sitting on the suitcase
shots.seen: The same picture, a little closer, one cut later. Timo is now laughing as hard as Luna, his eyes squeezed into happy lines, one fist punched high in the air; his other hand still holds her shoulder. Luna's arms are still up and she is still laughing. The street streaks past behind them.
shots.heard: none (no words). Natural sound: Timo's scream has turned into a big laugh, Luna whooping, wheels roaring. Music: the group "oh-oh-oh" and the claps come in.
shots.caption: none

shots.place: Near the bottom of the same street: the top of a garden wall in golden sun, soft painted houses behind it.
shots.who: The ginger cat; Luna and Timo only as a streak
shots.seen: The ginger cat again, sitting on top of a wall, calm, eyes half closed. Below it the yellow suitcase with the two friends on it shoots past from right to left: a streak of yellow, coral and teal. The wind flattens the cat's ears and blows its fur and whiskers to the left. Its head whips round after them. Its eyes are huge.
shots.heard: none (no words). Natural sound: a fast rattle of wheels and two laughing voices rushing past, a gust of wind, then one small surprised "mrrow". Music: drops to shaker and tick-tock for this one shot.
shots.caption: none

shots.place: The open space in front of the stadium, low golden sun from the left. Behind the friends the entrance is a bright warm glow under flags, with a few still, soft shapes of fans holding scarves up. At the left edge, soft, a small striped hut with shelves of bags.
shots.who: Luna and Timo
shots.seen: Framed like the first shot: Luna on the left, the yellow suitcase in the middle, Timo on the right, with the glowing stadium entrance behind them. The suitcase stands still, and a last puff of dust drifts away from its wheels. Timo is on his knees with his chest against the suitcase and both arms spread wide along its lid, holding its two corners. He looks up, beaming, and speaks. Then he lays his cheek on the lid and closes his eyes, smiling. Luna leans on the lid from her side with her arms folded, laughing into her arms so that only her crescent eyes show. She looks down at him and says something, her shoulders shaking. Timo, eyes shut, hugs the suitcase tighter.
shots.heard: Timo: "I love this suitcase." Then Luna, laughing: "Timo. This is the small one." Natural sound: Luna's big laugh, not cut clean; a happy sigh from Timo; the stadium roar swelling. Music: the hook runs to the last three claps.
shots.caption: I love this suitcase. (then, alone, after it has gone) Timo. This is the small one.

pilot.end_card: Two seconds on a plain warm cream card: the word VENUVOY in deep violet in the middle, the teal-and-coral trip scarf lying flat under it like an underline, and two small words below: "football trips". Sound: the last three claps of the theme, the final clap ending dry. No logo animation, no app, no link, no slogan. The card cuts straight back to frame one (the yellow suitcase in the station square), so the film loops. Shots 26 seconds plus card: 28 seconds.

production_notes: FOUR GATES BEFORE ANY FILM CLIP IS PAID FOR. (1) Look gate: one line-up still of Timo, Luna, Big Yellow and the cat, one 4-second speaking clip of each friend, and the two ride stills. Show the line-up to three people aged 18 to 25 and ask only 'who is this made for?'. If anyone says 'kids', fix the still (longer legs, smaller eyes, more real fabric), not the video. The client approves this picture before anything else is made. (2) Strip gate: all seven start pictures (nine with the second ride still and the cat streak still) laid side by side must tell the story with no text. (3) Silent gate: the finished cut, muted and with captions covered, goes to a real viewer of 18 to 25 and to an adult with English as a second language; it is published only if their one sentence matches the retell. (4) Fault gate: every clip is checked edge to edge and on its last frame. A faulty clip is generated again, never patched.

ORDER OF MAKING. First the two ride clips (shots 4 and 5): they are the go or no-go for the whole film. Then shot 7 (the payoff), then shot 3, then shots 1, 2 and 6. If the ride cannot be made clean in the chest-up framing after the plan B below, stop and report before spending on the rest.

VOICES, ONE PIPELINE. Before any video, record in one session per friend, in the two locked voices: Timo's three lines, Luna's one line, and a small library of sounds that are not words (Luna: laugh in three sizes, giggle, whoop, puffing; Timo: puffing, the long scream that turns into a laugh, a big laugh, a happy sigh). The lips in shots 1, 3 and 7 are driven from this audio; nothing spoken is taken from a generated clip. One outdoor room tone lies under all lines. Each voice is pinned to one approved reference clip in plain international English; no accent is left to chance. The same library serves every later film.

REFERENCE SHEETS. Each friend: front, side and a plain back view, plus expressions including the open scream and the open laugh (the two faces furthest from neutral). Big Yellow: its own sheet with fixed size (top level with Luna's chest), satin finish, two wide ridges, the short fixed handle on the front end, deep-violet wheels. The cat: front, side, back. Timo's skin tone is compared across all start pictures side by side, and again after the grade.

CHECKLIST FOR EVERY START PICTURE. Exact pixel size of the video model's 9:16 output (a slightly different shape is what causes a band). Luna left, Timo right. Sun low on screen left. Watch on Timo's real left wrist (in a back view that is the other screen side). Timo's scarf knotted and short, Luna's loose and long. Suitcase size against Luna's chest, handle on the front end, lid flat and empty. Plain shirt front and back, plain jacket with no sleeve stripes, plain backpack. No letters, numbers, clocks or sign-like shapes anywhere. No face inside the caption band (about two thirds of the way down). Coarse, soft fabric texture.

SHOT 1 (station). START PICTURE: everything already in place. The suitcase is parked in the middle with its wheels below the bottom edge of the frame. Luna has one hand flat on the lid, a closed-mouth smile, eyes on Timo. Timo is turned three-quarters to the camera with his face already towards the suitcase and his mouth closed; the arm without the watch is stretched out pointing up the street; the watch arm has its thumb under the backpack strap. The station is a plain arch with no clock; the train is only a soft shape. WHAT MOVES: Timo's eyes climb the suitcase, his arm sinks, his mouth opens, he says the line. Luna only breathes. Nothing rolls: the rattle and the bump are sound, laid on the first beat, and the single rock of the suitcase can be left out. PLAN B: if the line lands on Luna's mouth or goes soft, regenerate with Luna looking down at her suitcase; if it is still wrong, use the silent take (his mouth falls open) with the recorded line and the caption laid over it. If his arm does not sink, keep the take: a tall friend pointing the way at a giant suitcase still reads.

SHOT 2 (uphill, the cat overtakes). START PICTURE: side view, street climbing from right to left, friends from the knees up so feet and wheels are out of frame. Both are in held strain poses: Luna faces the suitcase and leans back with both hands on the front handle, in front of her body; Timo has both hands and one shoulder on the shell and his cheek already flat on it, face to the camera. The wall is on the far side with its top above all heads; the cat stands on it above Timo. WHAT MOVES: only the cat travels, along the top of the wall, in clear space above everyone, to a point ahead of Luna, and its one look back is its last move. The friends move a hand's width at most; Timo's eyes follow the cat and his cheek never lifts. Grinding wheels and slipping shoes are sound only. PLAN B: generate the cat alone on the wall and lay it over the friends' clip in the edit (it never overlaps them). If the walk fails twice, use three versions of the same still with the cat in three places (behind Timo, above the suitcase, ahead of Luna looking back), each held a little over a second: a hop that suits a handmade look. The cat is never cut from this shot, because shot 6 pays it off.

SHOT 3 (hilltop, the offer and the No). START PICTURE: camera on the hilltop at Luna's seated eye level, three-quarter view, so that the empty back half of the lid is in plain sight. The drop is painted clearly: roofs stepping down, the stadium below eye level in the gap between the friends, fans as still soft shapes. The suitcase stands on the last flat stones so it has no reason to creep. Luna already sits sideways on the front half, one arm already pointing at the stadium (held, it does not move), her other hand, the one nearest the camera, flat on the empty half of the lid. Timo stands on the right in profile with both palms already up. WHAT MOVES: her two pats in the first half of the clip, then his head shake, the words 'No, no, no' really spoken (a round open mouth is the easiest line to sync), and one step back. PLAN B: two clips from the same start picture (her pats, then his No) joined by a cut; or the line played over his shoulder with the head shake. If the pointing arm bends or doubles, remove it from the still: the stadium in the gap and the pat still tell it.

SHOTS 4 AND 5 (the ride). Two start pictures in the same framing, one clip each, so that no clip has to change an expression at a set moment. PICTURE A: chest up, the yellow lid only as a wide bar across the bottom (no knees), Luna's arms in a wide V fully inside the frame, Timo's whole face in the gap above her head, screaming, both hands on her shoulders (hands, not arms round her). PICTURE B: the same, a little closer; Timo laughing, the arm without the watch already up in a fist, the other hand on her shoulder. In both: hair stays solid, only scarves and shirts flap, scarf ends blown out to the sides and not across a face, walls painted as soft bands of colour with no doors, windows or signs. WHAT MOVES: a bounce, the flapping, the bands streaming outward. The cut from A to B lands on the beat where the voices come in. PLAN B: shorten each clip to 2 seconds; frame tighter on the two faces; if the racing camera invents scenery at the edges, generate both clips with a still camera against the painted bands and add the streaming in the edit. The scream and the laugh are laid from the voice library, not taken from the clips.

SHOT 6 (they pass the cat). START PICTURE: the cat alone, sitting on top of the wall in the upper half of the frame, facing us, eyes half closed; the lower half is only the wall and the street. WHAT MOVES: a gust from the right flattens its ears, blows fur and whiskers to the left, its head whips to the left, its eyes go huge. Still camera, one animal, no people. THE STREAK is made in the edit, not generated as video: an approved side-view still of both friends on the suitcase (Luna's arms up, Timo's fist up) slides from right to left across the lower half in about eight steps with a soft smear, never overlapping the cat. PLAN B: reduce the riders to three smeared bands of yellow, coral and teal for five frames; if the cat's reaction fails, keep only the head turn. Check the cat against shot 2: same shape, same plain coat, same wall colour.

SHOT 7 (the hug). START PICTURE: framed like shot 1, with the camera low enough that the lid sits a little above the middle of the frame and both faces are above the caption band. The hug is already in place: Timo on his knees, chest against the shell, both arms spread along the lid with his hands on the two near corners (not reaching all the way round), head up, beaming. Luna leans on the lid with folded arms and her mouth hidden in them, crescent eyes on Timo. Behind them: the entrance glow, flags, still soft fan shapes, the bag hut soft at the left edge. The dust puff is a layer added in the edit. WHAT MOVES: Timo says his line (lips from the recorded audio), lays his cheek down, closes his eyes; Luna's shoulders shake. Her line is laid in the edit and needs no lips at all, so it cannot land on the wrong mouth. Nobody touches the other, and no arm lands on anything. PLAN B: two start pictures (7a head up with the line, 7b cheek already down and eyes closing) joined on the beat. If Timo's lips fail, use only 7b with both recorded lines over it and the captions; the film is complete even on the silent hug. If the bag hut draws the eye or grows letter-like shapes, take it out of the still.

CHECK EVERY CLIP IN MOTION, NOT ONLY ITS START PICTURE. Letters and numbers appear during a clip in areas the still never showed: the frame edges of the ride, the stadium in shots 3 and 7, house doors, the back of the football shirt, the backpack, the trainers, the watch face. Look at the edges and at the last frame of every clip, and compare that last frame with the reference sheets: the drift goes towards a generic cartoon (bigger eyes, smoother skin, hair turning into strands, a rounder flat-top, a crest growing on the shirt). Reject, do not paint.
TRIMMING. Clips are generated at 5 to 6 seconds and cut down, so every prompt asks for the line and the key action in the first half of the clip.

COLOUR. Who is who rests on teal, coral and sunflower yellow staying apart. Golden light and a warm grade push yellow and coral towards orange and teal towards green, and in the ride the coral shirt sits directly on the yellow lid. Grade every film against the three fixed swatches.

THE STOP-MOTION STEP is tested before it is promised: apply 12 pictures a second to the ride clip and to one speaking clip. Generated clips carry motion blur and the step loosens lip sync, so if either test looks like a lagging video, the series stays smooth. If it passes, clips are generated with a still camera, stepped, and the hand wobble is added smoothly afterwards.

MUSIC. Delivered in layers at exactly 120 beats a minute before the edit begins. Hit points in the pilot: tick-tock on frame one, the bump on beat one, Luna's two pats on two beats, tick-tock alone on the No, the full groove on the cut into shot 4, the voices on the cut into shot 5, shaker and tick-tock only under the cat, the hook through shot 7, three claps and one dry beat on the card. Listen on a phone speaker before approving. If the sung 'oh-oh-oh' sounds artificial or grows word-like sounds, record it as a simple group shout.

CAPTIONS. One typeface, one size, one position, cream letters on a deep-violet plate (the band lies over the yellow suitcase in shots 1, 3 and 7, so a plate is needed). The band sits about two thirds of the way down, above the platform's own text and buttons. Each caption appears exactly on the first syllable of its line. In shot 7 the first caption leaves before the second arrives.

END CARD AND LOOP. The card holds two full seconds. The cut from the card to frame one is checked as part of the film: suitcase size, handle and sun side in shot 7 must match shot 1 exactly, because the two pictures follow each other in the loop.

POSTING. Every film carries the platform's AI label; with this look the label reads as a fact, not a confession. The post text holds what the film does not say: 'When your friend packs for one night.' and 'Plan or No Plan: which one are you?'.
decisions: CHANGE 1, the deadline is gone. The watch tapping in shot 1 and the line 'We have five minutes!' produced four separate guesses from all three viewers: is the problem the size or the time, five minutes until what, who is speaking from behind, did they make it on time. The film now has one physical idea: the same suitcase is painfully slow uphill and joyfully fast downhill. The watch stays on Timo's wrist as design and matters in later films (Top Row). If a test shows the pilot needs more urgency, it returns only as a picture (Timo showing his watch at the hilltop), never as a line.

CHANGE 2, shot 1 holds one idea. Timo's arm already points up the street to the floodlights (the want, as the clarity judge asked) and sinks while his eyes climb the suitcase (the thing in the way). A soft train behind the station arch shows they have just arrived, which answers 'one night where?' and why the suitcase comes straight to the ground. Following the risk review the suitcase is already parked, Luna keeps her mouth closed while he speaks, and the arch has no clock.

CHANGE 3, the old shot 2 (flat hand above her head) is cut: all three viewers had to guess the gesture, and it set up 'what is inside?' early and then dropped it. The line itself, which all three found funny, is kept and moved to the very end with his name in it: 'Timo. This is the small one.' That gives a second laugh after the hug, brackets the film with the first line ('Luna. It's one night!'), and fixes 'the tall guy's name is never said'. Luna's mouth is hidden in her arms, so the line needs no lip sync. Timo does not react to it, so nothing is lost when the text is covered.

CHANGE 4, the old shot 4 (suitcase rolls away by itself, lunge, catch) is replaced. It was marked high risk and two viewers said they could miss it. One hilltop picture now shows everything: the stadium in the gap between the friends, Luna already seated and pointing at it, patting the empty half of the lid, Timo refusing. The camera is raised and turned so the pats are visible, as the review asked. This also removes 'she is suddenly already sitting'.

CHANGE 5, the ride is built from two start pictures (scream, then laugh with the fist up) cut on the beat, the safer version from the review: chest up, lid as a bar, arms inside the frame, solid hair, soft bands for walls. The moment all three viewers called the warmest is kept exactly.

CHANGE 6, a new shot: they shoot past the cat. All three viewers named the cat as the best joke and said the film was predictable after the 'No'. The cat now gets its answer: it overtakes them uphill and they overtake it downhill, the same physical logic as the story. It is the safest clip in the film (one animal, still camera; the riders are a streak made in the edit).

CHANGE 7, the missing stop. All three felt a beat was missing between flying downhill and standing still. The cat shot now sits between the ride and the arrival, and the last shot opens on the suitcase standing in drifting dust with Timo on his knees. No stop is animated, because that is the kind of clip that fails.

CHANGE 8, the ending is made safe and stays one take: the hug is already in place in the start picture (no arm lands, no cheek arrives from far away), Timo speaks with his head up and only then lays it down, Luna's face is hidden while he speaks, both faces sit above the caption band, and nobody's arm goes round the other (safer, and it also answers 'friends or a couple?'). The watch check is removed, so nobody has to guess whether they were on time.

CHANGE 9, the bag hut. The fan viewer said no ground lets in a bag that size and two viewers asked why the suitcase goes to the stadium. A small hut with shelves of bags now stands soft in the background of the last shot and becomes a fixed part of the world: Big Yellow never enters a stadium.

CHANGE 10, the end card. All three viewers did not know what VENUVOY is, and the review found six words in 1.5 seconds too fast. The card now holds two seconds and the six-word line is replaced by two words, 'football trips'. This is a label, not a slogan; if the client wants the name alone, the two words move to the account line.

CHANGE 11, voices. Lip-synced lines drop from five to three, all by Timo, and every line and every laugh, scream and whoop is recorded first in one session per friend. The first version mixed lines from clips with lines laid in later, which is how voices changed in the first series.

CHANGE 12, design fixes from the review: a fixed short handle that never extends, a satin shell with few wide ridges, a plain jacket with no sleeve stripes, no one-sided details, the sun always on screen left, Luna always left and Timo always right, a plain back view on every reference sheet, the stop-motion step only after a test.

KEPT because it worked: the cat overtaking them, the 'No' followed by the hard cut, the scream that turns into a laugh with the fist up, the hug with 'I love this suitcase', the looping first and last frame, two people only.

NOT CHANGED on purpose: the fan viewer found the invented club generic. Real clubs, colours and grounds are ruled out by the brief. The answer is true fan behaviour instead: scarves held up, stand claps in the theme, the bag hut, and later films built on the chant, the first sight of the pitch and the morning with no voice.

CHOSEN: 'Plan, No Plan' (the duo) taken whole as the series. It had the highest cold-viewer scores (understood 9.33, enjoyed 8.33), the cleanest cause and effect according to the clarity judge, and it is the safest to make: two people, a dry sunny pilot, nothing that opens or changes shape.

FROM 'Away Crew': the art-toy look in streetwear instead of clay puppets, the caption discipline (no header, only the spoken line, one text at a time), hand-overs written as cuts, the suitcase with its own reference sheet, the hardest clip generated first, the trip scarf as the community's badge on the end card, and the film 'No Voice'.

FROM 'Trip Trip Hooray': the ginger cat as the recurring local, the rule that every sound that matters has a picture double, the silent-retell gate, and human sounds laid in from a library instead of taken from clips.

FROM 'First Away': the strip of start pictures as a gate before any video, the stop-motion step as an optional finish, and the first sight of the pitch as the one film with a lump in the throat (shown only as light on two faces).

REJECTED: three friends (three in frame plus rain is where the faults came from last time, and the trio pilots left viewers asking who the third person was); the 'When your friend' header and the 'Mission' header (reading load, brand-meme feel, a number that suggests a missed film); the selfie format (three camera modes, a fake vlogger, distorted faces); a fully wordless series (no voices means nobody to quote or to know); anything coming out of the suitcase in the pilot (opening lids, rain, a second costume); glasses, odd socks, a one-sided hair streak and sleeve stripes (details that mirror or multiply).

ROTATION across the season so nobody becomes the fool: Luna's way wins in One Night and Try It, Timo's planning wins in Wake Up, Luna and Just In Case, both are needed in The Clap, Top Row and No Voice, and the 'No' is said by each of them in turn.
